pure-announcement.rationale: It announces CodeRabbit's own report and ends in a product pitch, but the post substantively summarizes the findings and category-targeted guardrail recommendations, which transfer to any team reviewing AI-authored code.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts (evals, MCP, code retrieval) do not touch AI-versus-human code-defect rates or review guardrails, so nothing in the corpus covers this.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims trace to a linked report with a stated methodology and disclosed limitations, so a reader can check what was measured even though independent reproduction is limited.

durability.rationale: The headline rate ratios (1.7x overall, 2.74x security, ~8x excessive I/O) are point-in-time measurements of current model generations built on a self-admittedly unverifiable authorship-labeling heuristic, so the numbers will drift even if the amplification pattern holds.

actionability.rationale: The recommendations are concrete team actions targeted at the amplified categories — policy-as-code for style, mandated nullability and exception rules, centralized credential handling, and AI-aware reviewer checklists for error paths and concurrency.

atomicity.rationale: One central claim carries the whole note — AI-authored PRs show the same issue categories as human ones but at materially higher rates, so guardrails should target the amplified categories — and the ten findings are facets of it.
